content:
Factor \(891=3^4\cdot 11\). We need the smallest \(K\) such that
\[
10^K \equiv 1 \pmod{891}.
\]
Since \(\gcd(10,891)=1\), find the order of \(10\) modulo \(891\).

- Modulo \(11\): \(10\equiv -1\), so \(10^2\equiv 1\). Thus order modulo \(11\) is \(2\).
- Modulo \(81=3^4\): \(10=1+9\), so
\[
10^K=(1+9)^K\equiv 1+9K \pmod{81}.
\]
Thus \(10^K\equiv 1\pmod{81}\) iff \(9K\equiv 0\pmod{81}\), i.e. \(K\) is divisible by \(9\). So order modulo \(81\) is \(9\).

Therefore the order modulo \(891\) is
\[
\operatorname{lcm}(2,9)=18.
\]
Thus the smallest value is
\[
\boxed{18}.
\]
